summary: Revised analysis addresses both blocking issues from the first review: artifact inventory is now complete (8 bash scripts, related workflows identified) and HITL registration failure has been properly escalated as a recoverable infrastructure error.
analysis: The revised draft (v2) addresses all blocking feedback from the first review cycle. (1) Artifact inventory is now complete: lines 32-50 correctly identify on-check-failure.yml and reusable-autofix.yml as additional affected workflows, and list all 8 bash prompt builders including build-autofixer-prompt.sh and build-doc-updater-prompt.sh with a clear note that scripts 7 and 8 are out of the issue's stated scope but must be addressed. Line 50 correctly distinguishes that build-doc-updater-prompt.sh serves a workflow NOT being replaced. Lines 52-56 accurately list all 4 files referencing gha_exec(). (2) HITL registration: The refiner appropriately escalated the contract initialization failure as a recoverable error (line 156). The decisions are well-documented in the analysis and can be registered once the infrastructure issue is resolved — this is an acceptable workaround. (3) Decision 1 has been reframed from the redundant architecture question to the trigger mechanism question — the analysis no longer second-guesses the issue's stated concurrent BRC direction. New Decision 3 (reusable-autofix.yml fate) and Decision 6 (bash script scope) were added to cover previously unaddressed gaps. Decision 5 now recommends conditional criteria (Option B) for review consolidation, which is well-reasoned. The options analysis, constraints section, and complexity assessment all remain strong from v1 and have been updated with accurate counts (8 scripts, 4 gha_exec files). The complexity assessment now includes concrete workstream breakdowns with file estimates. All codebase claims verified in v1 remain accurate in v2.
suggestions: 1. The analysis could benefit from a brief section on rollback strategy — if the one-shot cutover fails, what is the recovery path? The issue proposes no parallel operation period, so the rollback plan is important. 2. Consider adding a note about testing strategy: the issue mentions validating the babysit-pr cycle against the cutover PR itself, but doesn't discuss how to test the trigger mechanism before committing to the cutover. 3. Feedback Question 3 now correctly references reusable-autofix.yml's header comment about external repos — good improvement.
